title: Settings
precipitationRangeDescription: Defines how many hours in advance the next precipitation should appear
error_building_item: Could not load this item's information.

general.title: General
general.language: Change the language used throughout the app
general.location: Location used for weather and the clock's time zone
general.aqiScale: Sets the standard used to classify and display air quality index levels.

betaCity.name: Beta City
betaCity.desc: Test city: real Toronto weather with temperature going from {{from}}°C to {{to}}°C in {{hours}}h.

radius.title: Radius (km)
radius.description: Maximum distance to search for weather alerts

status.title: Status
status.updatedAtDesc: Time of the last weather refresh

sunAlertThresholdMinutes.title: Sun Alert Lead Time
sunAlertThresholdMinutes.desc: Sets how many minutes before sunrise or sunset the icons should be displayed. The icon will only appear in clear weather.

showFeelsLikeWhenEqual.title: Redundant Feels Like
showFeelsLikeWhenEqual.desc: Displays the feels-like temperature even when its value equals the current temperature. If disabled, the field is hidden in this condition.

showMinMaxPeakBadge.title: Current Min/Max Indicator
showMinMaxPeakBadge.desc: Displays the "MIN" or "MAX" labels when the current temperature exactly reaches the day's forecast minimum or maximum.

focusCurrentWeatherOnLaunch.title: Focus Current Weather on Launch
focusCurrentWeatherOnLaunch.desc: Sets whether the app should open with the current weather section selected and highlighted by default.

hourlyForecastInFocus.title: Hourly Forecast in Focus
hourlyForecastInFocus.desc: Shows the hourly forecast inside the current weather section (highlighted), below the precipitation chart. When off, it stays below the section.

is12hour.title: Time format
is12hour.desc: Use AM and PM instead of the 24-hour format.

useBottomSheet.title: Use Bottom Sheet
useBottomSheet.desc: Displays details and windows at the bottom of the screen (Bottom Sheet) instead of a central window (Modal).

hourlyForecastView.title: Next hours
hourlyForecastView.desc: Shows the forecast for the next hours as cards or as a temperature chart.

alerts.title: Weather alerts
alerts.desc: National Weather Service (US) and Environment and Climate Change Canada

impact.veryStrong: Can significantly affect movement and outdoor activities.

humidityTextes.veryDry: Very dry. You may notice dryness and irritation.

humidityTextes.extremelyHumid: Extremely humid. Expect oppressive conditions and excessive moisture.

dewPointTexts.veryDry: Very dry air. The air feels crisp and dry.
dewPointTexts.dryAndComfortable: Dry and comfortable. Humidity is low but generally pleasant.
dewPointTexts.comfortable: Comfortable. The air feels dry and pleasant.
dewPointTexts.veryComfortable: Very comfortable. Humidity is barely noticeable.
dewPointTexts.slightlyComfortable: Comfortable, with a slight hint of humidity.
dewPointTexts.slightlyHumid: Slightly humid. You may start noticing some moisture in the air.
dewPointTexts.humid: Humid. The air may start feeling sticky or uncomfortable.
dewPointTexts.veryHumid: Very humid. Expect muggy and uncomfortable conditions.
dewPointTexts.oppressive: Oppressive humidity. The air feels extremely muggy and heavy.

daylightTextes.short: A short day with limited daylight.
daylightTextes.balanced: Day and night are nearly balanced.
daylightTextes.long: A long day with plenty of daylight.
daylightTextes.veryLong: A very long day with an extended evening.
daylightTextes.exceptionallyLong: An exceptionally long day with daylight lasting for many hours.

sunshineTextes.veryLittle: Very little sunshine. Expect mostly cloudy conditions.
sunshineTextes.limited: Limited sunshine. The sun may appear only occasionally.
sunshineTextes.moderate: Some sunshine. Expect a mix of sun and clouds.
sunshineTextes.plenty: Plenty of sunshine. The sun should be noticeable for much of the day.
sunshineTextes.verySunny: A very sunny day with long periods of sunshine.
sunshineTextes.exceptionallySunny: An exceptionally sunny day with nearly uninterrupted sunshine.

clear.description: Favourable conditions. No major rain or strong wind expected.

severeWind.description: Very strong winds without rain. Watch for loose objects and falling branches.

strongWind.description: A very windy day without rain. Take extra care when walking outdoors.

moderateBreeze.description: Moderate winds without rain. Conditions are generally comfortable outdoors.

heavyRain.description: Intense rain with little wind. Bring an umbrella or waterproof clothing.

moderateRain.description: Steady rain without strong winds. An umbrella should be enough.

lightDrizzle.description: Only light drizzle with little wind. Conditions remain manageable outdoors.

storm.description: Heavy rain combined with very strong winds. Avoid going outside if possible.

windDrivenRain.description: Strong winds are blowing the rain sideways. Umbrellas may be difficult to use, so waterproof clothing is recommended.

rainWithWind.description: Rain accompanied by wind gusts. Waterproof outerwear is recommended.

legend.conversionInfo: Concentrations are provided in µg/m³ and converted to {{unit}} based on the molecular weight of each pollutant, as well as the air temperature and pressure at the time of the reading.

us.good: Air quality is satisfactory, and the risk is minimal or nonexistent.
us.fair: Air quality is acceptable. Extremely sensitive individuals should consider reducing prolonged outdoor exertion.
us.moderate: People with respiratory or heart conditions, older adults, and children may experience effects. The general public is unlikely to be affected.
us.poor: Everyone may begin to experience health effects. Sensitive groups may experience more serious impacts.
us.veryPoor: Health alert: everyone is at increased risk of experiencing adverse health effects. Avoid outdoor activities.
us.extremelyPoor: Emergency warning: the entire population is at high risk of serious health impacts. Remain indoors.

eu.good: Air quality is considered ideal for most people.
eu.fair: Air quality is acceptable. Enjoy your usual outdoor activities.
eu.moderate: Sensitive individuals experiencing symptoms should consider reducing strenuous outdoor activities.
eu.poor: Unhealthy air quality. Sensitive groups should reduce outdoor physical activities.
eu.veryPoor: Everyone should consider reducing their time outdoors.
eu.extremelyPoor: Critical warning: minimize outdoor exposure and avoid exercising outdoors.

eu.good: Ideal fine particle levels. Zero risk of deep lung penetration.
eu.fair: Acceptable PM2.5 level. Enjoy your normal outdoor activities.
eu.moderate: People with respiratory issues may experience minor discomfort from microparticles.
eu.poor: Moderate to high risk: fine particles can irritate the respiratory tract of sensitive groups.
eu.veryPoor: High PM2.5 concentration. Everyone should avoid prolonged physical exertion outdoors.
eu.extremelyPoor: Dangerous microparticle level. Stay indoors with filtered air whenever possible.

us.good: Insignificant fine particle concentration. No health risks.
us.fair: Unusually sensitive people to PM2.5 should consider reducing prolonged physical exertion.
us.moderate: Sensitive groups may experience symptoms like coughing and shortness of breath. General public usually unaffected.
us.poor: Significant increase in lung irritation risk for everyone. At-risk groups should stay indoors.
us.veryPoor: Severe PM2.5 alert: high risk of respiratory and cardiac complications. Avoid all outdoor activity.
us.extremelyPoor: Emergency fine particle levels. Keep doors and windows closed and use air purifiers.

eu.good: Inhalable particle concentration at a safe and ideal level.
eu.fair: Low presence of dust and inhalable particles. Normal conditions for the general public.
eu.moderate: People with asthma or allergies may experience minor eye or throat irritation.
eu.poor: Poor air quality due to dust and particles. At-risk groups should limit outdoor time.
eu.veryPoor: High PM10 levels. Recommended to limit outdoor activities to reduce dust inhalation.
eu.extremelyPoor: Critical particle concentration in the air. Everyone should avoid exposure and keep windows closed.

us.good: Insignificant level of inhalable particles in the air.
us.fair: Acceptable air quality with low presence of dust and particle pollution.
us.moderate: People with lung disease, older adults, and children should reduce prolonged outdoor exertion.
us.poor: Increased risk of respiratory discomfort for the general public and serious symptoms in sensitive individuals.
us.veryPoor: Unhealthy conditions: risk of severe airway irritation. Avoid staying outdoors.
us.extremelyPoor: Emergency PM10 alert. High concentration of dust and soot; avoid any outdoor exposure.

eu.good: Ideal ground-level ozone levels. Clean, pure air.
eu.fair: Ozone presence within normal safety standards.
eu.moderate: People with asthma should monitor potential throat irritation when exercising outdoors.
eu.poor: Elevated ozone level. Sensitive groups should avoid strenuous physical activity in the afternoon.
eu.veryPoor: High ground-level ozone concentration. Reduce outdoor exposure time, especially on warm days.
eu.extremelyPoor: Emergency ozone warning: high risk of lung inflammation. Stay indoors.

us.good: No risk of ground-level ozone exposure.
us.fair: Acceptable air quality. Unusually sensitive people may experience minor discomfort by late afternoon.
us.moderate: Children, older adults, and outdoor exercisers may experience reduced lung capacity.
us.poor: Risk of eye and airway irritation for the general public. Avoid outdoor activities during peak hours.
us.veryPoor: Very high ozone levels. Health alert for the entire population; avoid leaving home.
us.extremelyPoor: Severe risk of respiratory damage. Stay indoors with air conditioning.

eu.good: Minimal nitrogen dioxide concentration. Excellent air quality.
eu.fair: Acceptable NO2 level, originating mainly from light urban traffic.
eu.moderate: People with chronic respiratory conditions may notice mild airway sensitivity.
eu.poor: Elevated NO2 level. People with asthma or bronchitis should avoid heavy traffic.
eu.veryPoor: High NO2 pollution. Everyone should avoid prolonged exposure in heavy traffic areas.
eu.extremelyPoor: Critical nitrogen dioxide level. Avoid leaving home and keep indoors ventilated if far from traffic.

us.good: No health impacts associated with nitrogen dioxide.
us.fair: Acceptable NO2 level with no obvious risks for most people.
us.moderate: Individuals with asthma may experience increased respiratory symptoms near busy roads.
us.poor: Increased risk of respiratory infections and inflammation. Sensitive groups should stay home.
us.veryPoor: Health alert: high risk of bronchitis and severe asthma attacks. Avoid traffic and industrial areas.
us.extremelyPoor: Dangerous NO2 levels. Risk of severe impacts on lung function for the entire population.

eu.good: Insignificant sulphur dioxide level. Clean air quality.
eu.fair: SO2 concentration within safe emission limits.
eu.moderate: People with asthma may experience mild discomfort when breathing deeply.
eu.poor: Elevated SO2 level. Sensitive people should avoid the outdoors, especially near industrial zones.
eu.veryPoor: High sulphur concentration in the air. Everyone should limit outdoor time.
eu.extremelyPoor: Critical SO2 level. Risk of immediate bronchospasm in asthmatics; stay indoors.

us.fair: Acceptable and safe SO2 level for the general population.
us.moderate: People with asthma during physical activity may experience wheezing and shortness of breath.
us.poor: The general public may begin to feel throat and eye irritation. At-risk groups should avoid going out.
us.veryPoor: Health alert: dangerous sulphur dioxide concentration. Completely avoid outdoor activities.
us.extremelyPoor: Health emergency for SO2: risk of severe respiratory tract damage for anyone.

us.good: Low CO levels. Under normal conditions, health risk is minimal.
us.fair: Moderately elevated CO. People with heart disease may be more sensitive, especially during physical exertion.
us.moderate: Elevated CO levels. Sensitive people may experience headache, fatigue, or shortness of breath; reduce prolonged exertion.
us.poor: Unhealthy CO level. May cause headache, dizziness, nausea, and weakness. Limit prolonged exposure.
us.veryPoor: Very high CO. May cause dizziness, confusion, nausea, and loss of coordination. Avoid exposure and seek fresh air.
us.extremelyPoor: Dangerously high CO. May cause severe poisoning, loss of consciousness, or death. Move away from the source and seek fresh air immediately.
